source.inventory_method: Distinct MQTT-* identifiers from HTML text; official typo MQTT-3-8.3-4 retained verbatim. Not an exhaustive inventory of unnumbered normative requirements.

claim: Targeted scenario evidence only; mapped clauses are not complete normative conformance approval. Unmapped clauses stay NotRun. Complete F6 remains Partial.

scenarios.scope: Unsupported protocol and empty persistent ID return CONNACK then close; pipelined PUBLISH must not route. Mixed listeners reject cross-protocol Session resume before fencing; explicit clean replacement is supported.
Reserved flags, Will flags and missing or unflagged payload fields: close without CONNACK.
Representative invalid flags, empty filters, invalid QoS/ID/topic UTF8 and first/second CONNECT violations close only offender.
Replace QoS, replay retained, exact filter deletion and UNSUBACK even when no filter removed; new live traffic stops after unsubscribe.
Pipelined PUBLISH IDs 9,2,7; reversed and duplicate PUBREC with a one-frame control budget; deterministic no-writer-progress fixture.
Preserve reverse PUBREC order and remaining PUBLISH identifiers/order/DUP across snapshot and actual SQLite restart.
Accept alphanumeric IDs at every length 1..23 with configured minimum; preserve BOM, Unicode forms, case, spaces and empty levels.

Method B duplicate/release/identifier reuse and changed duplicate content: never route accepted QoS2 twice. Receiver ownership matrix additionally covers two states x four events x memory/snapshot recovery, including retained replacement and post-PUBCOMP ID reuse. Actual TCP/SQLite matrix: both protocols x in-process reconnect/restart x repeated DUP=0/1, preserving original Retained payload/properties, repeated PUBREL and post-PUBCOMP reuse.

Both reconnect phases preserve IDs; wrong ACK/PUBCOMP cannot free pending PUBLISH; window enforces PUBLISH order. Supplemental literal-wire sender ACK phase matrix across two SQLite restarts; original Packet ID/DUP, payload and subsequent delivery preserved. Includes mixed MQTT5 counterpart; finite cases, not full conformance. Extra MQTT5-style reason/properties bytes on3.1.1 ACKs close the offender without completing QoS1 or advancing QoS2; SQLite recovery preserves original ownership and subsequent delivery.
Abrupt-close QoS2 retained Will and late subscriber replay use full outgoing handshake.

Handshake timeout, keepalive expiration triggers Will, fragmented frames make progress. PING on an independent idle connection progresses while Store holds another connection; same-connection PING cannot overtake durable PUBREC.
Abrupt close and takeover publish Will; graceful DISCONNECT removes it.
Offline reliable messages survive disconnect and retransmit using original IDs and DUP.
One SUBSCRIBE ID0x1234 with duplicate filters and denial: SUBACK codes retain input order; retained replays use both grants and final live QoS uses replacement.
All nine publish/subscription QoS combinations preserve arbitrary binary payload; incoming DUP does not propagate; QoS0 emits no ACK/PacketID and server DUP0.
QoS2->0->1 retained replacement; live RETAIN0 vs replay RETAIN1; ordinary and empty RETAIN0 leave old value; empty RETAIN1 removes it and still forwards empty payload.
UNSUBACK original ID; unsubscribing stops new routing while previously started QoS1 and QoS2 exchanges complete.
CleanSession1 takeover clears both QoS2 directions and subscriptions, keeps retained; next persistent connection is empty, following takeover resumes Session Present1.
Sixteen TCP matching traces cover empty levels, parent #, complete + levels, case, spaces, literal colon and leading-dollar isolation; malformed multi-filter packets apply no prefix.
65535-byte three-byte UTF8 Topic and exact filter work over TCP and retained replay under explicitly sufficient packet budget.
NUL, invalid UTF8 and surrogate encodings in ClientID/WillTopic/username/SUB/UNSUB close; binary password parses and reaches authentication rejection.
All QoS0/1/2 x retain0/1 combinations preserve binary Will payload, live and late delivery flags; no-Will DISCONNECT stays silent.

Forced65535->1 wrap skips occupied QoS1/2 IDs including Release; only correctly completed ID is reused. Simultaneous receiver/sender PacketID1 stays independent. Supplemental literal TCP/SQLite: both protocols x two outbound QoS2 phases x two completion orders, same inbound/outbound ID across two restarts; changed duplicates do not route, completing one namespace preserves the other, post-completion reuse and subsequent output work. Same-ID duplex fault intersections:24 commit-before-failure/lost-receipt/resolution-unavailable cases across both protocols/two sender phases/two directions,16 one-byte partial PUBREC/PUBCOMP cancellation/EOF cases and4 Unix real two-SIGKILL cases; independent durable phase/completion and reuse preserved. Not hardware power-loss or all fault combinations.
After persistent disconnect, QoS1 and QoS2 are accepted into offline subscriptions; reconnect SessionPresent1, same order and independent Packet IDs, complete exchanges.
Wrong protocol name closes without CONNACK; rejected24-byte ID returns2, forbidden Will returns5, exhausted disconnected Session quota returns3; no failure creates a Session.
Empty clean ClientID receives a fresh noncolliding identity; existing session cannot be taken over by server assignment.
QoS3 PUBLISH is rejected locally without restarting Core.
Overlapping subscriptions deliver one copy at highest matching QoS; PUBREL fixed bits and ACK IDs/lengths validated.
Original QoS2 participates in ACL; denied PUBLISH closes without admission; reliable saturation rejects whole publication without affecting independent connections.
Table3.1 wire frames distinguish rejected ID, server storage unavailable and authorization; unclassified failures produce no CONNACK.
Independent rumqttc client uses only MQTT3.1.1 over TCP; fragmented/coalesced packets preserve ordered byte-stream behavior.

39 independent Modorch topic vectors normalized to JSON drive Core validation/matching, the pinned Facade helper, actual Hub subscriptions/Handler delivery and real MQTT TCP validation/routing. $share is literal in 3.1.1. No magicCommon execution or MQTT5 sharing is claimed.
All 256 first bytes against type/direction/flags; 256 CONNECT flags against syntax/anonymous credentials; exact reserved CONNACK bits. Malformed header rejection isolates the client.

Remaining Length boundary prefixes and budgets, exact decoder input, mandatory ID0/1/65535, illegal length/header rejection before body and persistent-session/Will cleanup. Not a full wire-layout proof.
All 12 Server sender ACK transitions across Empty/Queued/AwaitPubRec/AwaitPubComp preserve owned ID/payload until proper completion; PUBREC including duplicates emits one PUBREL.

KeepAlive1 expires during Publish/Subscribe authorization; late grants do not admit retained data or subscriptions. Supplemental local policy tests cover principal expiry (including long/unlimited lifetimes).

TCP/TLS network closes on KeepAlive during Store commit/gate wait, while accepted QoS2 work drains without poisoning or rerouting. Supplemental implementation policies cover CONNECT deadline, mid-frame write deadline despite PING traffic, and checked shutdown during committed receipt wait; those policies are not additional MQTT normative obligations.

Independent literal output bytes for nine implemented Server packet kinds: CONNACK session/rejection contexts, ACK identifiers1/256/65535, mixed SUBACK, binary/UTF8 PUBLISH flags, retained/live/retry and RL127/128/16383/16384. Limited matrix; not all FSM/fault/platform combinations. Mixed-protocol one-byte transport confirms FIFO partial control writes and MQTT311 isolation from MQTT5 negotiation.

One-byte duplex stalls a partially written QoS1/2 PUBLISH until local write timeout; memory session keeps ownership and reconnect emits exact original ID/DUP and completes handshake. Deterministic stream fault, not kernel/TLS/storage or scheduler timing certification. Supplemental mixed-version partial control ACK interruption/resume/clean-rebuild matrix returns all owned memory; no process crash simulated.

Real TCP window1/backlog2: stalled PUBCOMP plus queued Publish exhausts reliable target; new retained QoS2 is rejected before PUBREC without partial fanout or ghost receiver. Drain and same-ID retry route once. Local policy atomic admission; not production slow-consumer/RSS/SLO approval.

Mixed listener accepts and recovers legal 3.1.1/5.0 packet-size boundaries for retained, reliable outgoing and incoming QoS2 ownership; retained publisher identity survives recovery. Targeted evidence, not full mixed-version conformance. Includes offline 3.1.1 delivery of alias-expanded MQTT5 messages after an explicit listener limit increase; recovery also succeeds at the original ingress limit.

MQTT-2.3.1-2.reason: Client chooses unused Packet IDs; server inheritance is covered by MQTT-2.3.1-4.

MQTT-3.1.2-23.reason: Client sends PINGREQ when no other control packet is sent.

MQTT-3.1.3-7.reason: Client supplying empty ClientID must set CleanSession1; server rejection is covered separately.

MQTT-3.14.4-1.reason: Client closes after sending DISCONNECT; server receiving obligations are in3.14.4-3.

MQTT-3.14.4-2.reason: Client sends no further packets after DISCONNECT.

MQTT-4.5.0-2.reason: Client acknowledges PUBLISH regardless of matching subscriptions.
